Definition: {to be (causative) make well, literally (sound, beautiful) or figuratively (happy, successful, right)}
BiblicalUsage: The word yᵉṭab carries the sense of to seem good, to be well. In Ezra 7:18, whatsoever shall seem good to thee.
TheologicalSignificance: Artaxerxes leaves the choice to what seems good, and I take yᵉṭab as a reminder that God works through ordinary human judgment too.
